issues.cell: Part L law 1 (2) (adj l. 422-431: the forms by level 'read from what stands', 'a crossing that fits neither form is unlawful', PRB7F-GEN-03, -TIM-02) x *standing span* (adj l. 337-338) x law 1 (5)'s fallen span (adj l. 440-442) x *The soft readings* (adj l. 495-499) x law 1 (10)'s condition exception (adj l. 461-462) x law 2 (c) (adj l. 556-561); W1 at an epoch, W4, W5, W8, W10, W12 x C3-C5, C10, C11; item 114
issues.claim: Pass 6 made law 1 (2)'s form a function of the channel's level against 'the wall's top' and 'height' and of 'the aqueduct's arch or pier there', read from what stands, and added 'a crossing that fits neither form is unlawful' - but Part L defines none of these against condition, while law 2 (c) lets every op but a frame growth wait. The set gives two tops: the section (Enceinte.heightCm / walls.barriers class row above its base, base l. 2262-2263; what stands of a wall 'whatever its condition', adj l. 311-312) and the run as readers have it ('a breached or dismantled run a gap for every reader', base l. 2492-2493; glTF 'no prism', base l. 16038; E-R2 ties casters and exports to law 1 (7)'s top). (1) A run beneath a merged pier breached by decay (V06 §3.7.7), neglect, the pathway's dismantling or a landfall (V05 l. 1338, 1342): by the section it stays merged (W4/W5/W12·C2 unchanged meeting; T-V6-73 asserts the run decays to breached beneath the aqueduct); by the run it reads over with a standing pier in the band - neither form - so the decay waits for ever (against item 114) and the landfall has no lawful outcome. (2) A founding across a breached run (W1·C11; T110-2 (1)): by the run's top an arch clearing only the gap is lawful, and the run's repairWall (item 114's recovery) then fits neither form and waits for ever. (3) A merged arch fallen or its pier cleared (V06 §3.19.2 (3)-(4), V05 l. 1342): nothing stands to build round - merged vacuously (C5's band whole) or neither, the strike, topple and landfall waiting. (4) A circuit laid at an epoch under a fallen span is checked against 'every standing span' only; the span's later repair (V06 §3.19.2 (5), hand repairRaised) whose recorded soffit lies below the circuit's top while the channel lies above it fits neither form and waits for ever - though law 1 (5) reads a fallen span exactly so that a repair stands over nothing (adj l. 988-991; PRB7-14), and C10 and R7-06 (a)'s C10 run say the repaired span stands. Two outcomes on every merged crossing whose run decays; item 114 broken on one reading; pass 6's verdict named this attack (adj l. 3601-3603).
issues.required_change: Law 1 (2), adj l. 422-425: 'at the aqueduct's level, in the form that level there gives, read from what stands, nothing of either record written (J149): **over**, where its channel there lies above the wall's top - no standing support in the band there and every standing span above the band clearing the wall's top, the band passing beneath the arch; **merged**, where its channel lies within the wall's height - the band built up to and around the aqueduct's arch or pier there at the wall's own top,' -> 'at the aqueduct's level, in the form that level there gives, nothing of either record written (J149) - the level and the form read from the two records whatever either side's condition: the channel's level the deck's level there (RaisedWayRecord), the wall's top and height its section's there (the full curtain's or its stretch class's height above its base, §2.7), however its runs have worn, breached or been dismantled, and each span over the band by its recorded soffit, standing or fallen, as law 1 (5) reads a fallen span: **over**, where the channel there lies above the wall's top - no standing support in the band there and every span above the band clearing the wall's top, the band passing beneath the arch; **merged**, where the channel lies within the wall's height - the band built up to and around what stands there of the aqueduct's arch or pier at the wall's own top (where none stands - its span fallen, its support cleared - the band whole at its own top),'. Law 1 (2), after 'each keeping its own condition (item 114);' add: 'so no change of either side's condition - a fall, a clearing, a topple, decay, a breach, a dismantling, a landfall, a repair - changes the form a crossing takes or makes it unlawful (*The soft readings*);'. The check (adj l. 603-604), after '(3) by the stored *Order* of the lines that cross;' add: '(2) by the records' levels and soffits, never a run's condition or a span's state;'. Consequences: E-S13's T110-4 (a) adds a fixture whose aqueduct crosses a ring merged (channel within the ring's height, a pier in the band), run over the state sweep with W4, W5, W10 and W12 - decay, breach, dismantling, landfall and repair applying, the form unchanged; E-R2's readers keep drawing a breached run as a gap (for drawing only, never law 1 (2)'s).

issues.cell: Part L law 2 (c)'s frame-growth clause (adj l. 559-561) x law 2 (a) (adj l. 519-535) x law 1 (2)'s over clearance and law 1 (5)'s gate, postern or tower under an over arch, 'never on a support's ring' (adj l. 422-431, 440-442; J149) x the support step's (7) and (3) (base l. 2712-2724, 2534-2540); C12 x W1 at an epoch (the extension after the trace); E-V6-13
issues.claim: An aqueduct sourced beyond the frame ends on the outer ring (base l. 2793-2797); a stage ring laid after it crosses its end span over, the span clearing the ring's top and one of its towers or a gatehouse under it (law 1 (5)'s over crossing, admitted since J149). An epoch's frame growth re-lays that span from the last interior station ((7); §4.11, base l. 8564-8566): a new station can fall on the tower's or gatehouse's footprint beyond the band ((3) slides it off the band only and names no gate or tower), and the new span's crown moves, so on a falling channel its soffit (deck level at the crown less deckDepthCm, base l. 2294) can lie below the wall's or gate's top the old span cleared. The extension is the op's own structure; (a) may slide stations within the slide bound and fails where none clears; (b) moves only Tier-3 things; (c)'s clause for the one op that cannot wait covers only 'a bound no fitting course meets' (R7-04 (c): maxClearSpanM, maxPierM) with 'every obstacle' (3)'s list. The laws give no shape: a builder lays it with law 1 (2) or (5) false (§5.3's row fails), reports it under raised.extendedPastBound (E-V6-13: water or maxPierM only), or leaves the deck short of the new ring (T110-2: 'the deck reaching the new ring'). Pass 6's verdict listed 'a frame growth's end span over a high crossing' (adj l. 3601-3603).
issues.required_change: Law 2 (c), adj l. 559-561: 'the one op that cannot wait is a frame growth, whose extension keeps the deck's course past a bound no fitting course meets, each station placed off every obstacle but the one it fails, reported (raised.extendedPastBound).' -> 'the one op that cannot wait is a frame growth: its extension keeps the deck's course and, wherever a standing wall-like structure crosses the old end span, keeps that span as it stood - the old foot's point its first new station, every crossing's form and clearance and every gate, postern, tower and fixed place under it unchanged (law 1 (2), (5), (11)) -, laying its new stations beyond; past a bound no fitting course meets, each station placed off every obstacle but the one it fails, the footprints law 1 (5) names among the obstacles, reported (raised.extendedPastBound).' Consequences: the model's support step (7) (E-M1) and E-P8 cite it ('the old end span kept where a wall-like structure crosses it, §2.7's laws, law 2 (c)'); E-V6-13's comment adds 'or an old end span kept over a wall-like structure'; T110-2's frame clause adds the same aqueduct with a ring's tower under its end span.

issues.cell: Part L law 1 (11) (adj l. 464-468) and law 2 (a)'s 'standing as the commit began' (adj l. 520-521) x *commit* (an epoch one commit, adj l. 409-412) x the check (adj l. 603-604) x T110-4 (E-S13, adj l. 1905-1906); W1 at an epoch: V06 §3.2 rows 9 (fortification), 10a (raisedWays), 14 (growth) (V06 l. 1003-1010)
issues.claim: Law 1 (11) - J148's Tier 1 since pass 6 (PRB7F-TIM-03) - and the check hold only a gate, postern, tower or fixed place 'standing as a commit begins'. An epoch is one commit of nineteen steps: the fortification step (row 9) lays a contraction's ring with gates and towers, a quay wall's sea gates or a first harbour-mouth chain (V06 §3.7.6 (3)), and the same epoch's raisedWays founding (row 10a) or growth (row 14, a frame growth's extension among it) then meets them. Neither law 1 (11) nor law 2 (a)'s plan-round list reaches them, so a build that slides the new gate along its ring or the chain to other heads to keep a founded aqueduct's least-cost course - the move pass 5 withdrew - leaves law 1 (1)-(11) true at the epoch's end and passes §5.3's row and T110-4 ('no gate, postern, tower or fixed place moved for a meeting'). The class PRB7F-TIM-03 closed stays open for everything an epoch lays before its own later steps.
issues.required_change: Law 1 (11), adj l. 464-465: 'no gate, postern, tower or fixed place standing as a commit begins is moved or removed by a meeting: at its end each stands where it stood,' -> 'no gate, postern, tower or fixed place standing as a commit begins, or laid by an earlier op of that commit (at an epoch an earlier step's: a contraction's, a quay wall's or a harbour-mouth chain's at its fortification step, a new stage's at its growth step), is moved or removed by a meeting: at its end each stands where it stood or where that op laid it,'. Law 2 (a), adj l. 520-521: 'planned round every Tier-1 thing standing as the commit began that it does not lay again' -> 'planned round every Tier-1 thing standing as it acts - one an earlier op of the commit laid among them - that it does not lay again'. The check, adj l. 604: '(9) - (11) by what the commit made newly or moved, against what stood as it began;' -> '(9) - (11) by what the commit made newly or moved, against what stood as it began, and (11) also against the place each Tier-1 thing had when an earlier batch of the commit laid it (that batch's commit record);'. Consequence: E-S13's T110-4 (c) adds 'an epoch whose fortification step lays a contraction, a quay wall's sea gates or a harbour-mouth chain and whose raisedWays step founds a raised way across them - none of them moved'.

issues.claim: Pass 6 gave W6·C2 the case 'a gate it opens under an aqueduct's arch that clears it (law 1 (5)) becomes a junction there, its square ... read across the span's strip by law 1 (8) · T-V6-47', and W14·C2 the village REPLACEMENT waiting where 'its new top would rise past the soffit of an aqueduct's arch over a kept gate ... T-V7-48 (E)'. Neither named test holds a gate under an aqueduct's arch: T-V6-47's H-AQUA ring has 'no gate or tower in the under-deck strip' and E-V6-8 (2)'s W6 run 'no gate it opens under a deck'; T-V7-48 has '0 gates in an under-deck strip' and E-V7-1's REPLACEMENT run sets up no gate under the declared aqueduct. Each cell names a test that never sets up its state (R7-06's class), so the J149 cases run on no fixture.
issues.required_change: END lines citing §2.7's laws: V06 (E-V6-8 (2)'s W6 clause): '- no gate it opens under a deck' -> '- no gate it opens under a road deck; and on an H-AQUA variant whose CITY ring has a gate under an aqueduct span that clears it and the wall (§2.7's laws, law 1 (5)), the pathway opening it - a junction there, its square laid, the span read open while the square lies there, and after the run beneath is dismantled no chamber laid while it does (law 1 (8))'; V07 (E-V7-1, after its REPLACEMENT run): '; and on a variant whose palisade gate stands under the declared aqueduct's arch, the arch clearing the palisade and the gate but not the stone wall's top, the REPLACEMENT waiting (walls.waited), the palisade, its gate and the aqueduct unchanged (§2.7's laws, law 1 (5), law 2 (c))'.

issues.cell: law 4 (PRB7D-TIM-10's closure, adj l. 2961) x V11 row 863's raisedWays.structure.span exception (V11 l. 862-863) x E-V11-1 (adj l. 2652-2658) x T110-4 (c)'s drawn edits (adj l. 1895-1897) x V12's span-rule line (V12 l. 2188) x law 1 (2), (5), (7), (10)
issues.claim: Since PRB7F-GEN-03, law 1 (2)'s form and (5)'s clearance turn on each span's soffit (deck level at the crown less raisedWays.structure.span.deckDepthCm, base l. 2294) and on the wall's top (the curtain's values, walls.barriers' class rows, V07 §3.4's village rows); law 1 (7)'s cap and (10)'s 'no soffit lowered over a run of it' read the same soffit. Law 4 resolves every edit that changes a structure's geometry or section; but V11's item-110 pattern says 'a span edit re-runs the span rule ... and V04's arch-vault reconcile in the same commit' and keeps what it changes, E-V11-1's exception names only stripMarginM, §4.8's band and setback rows and palisade.bandM, T110-4 (c)'s drawn edits the same three, and V12's line names the support step, the span rule and V04 as deckDepthCm's readers. A deckDepthCm raise turns over crossings into neither and lowers the cap over a shape-locked run; the examples keep both.
issues.required_change: END lines citing §2.7's laws: V11 (E-V11-1's exception adds): 'raisedWays.structure.span's deckDepthCm (every span's soffit) and the rows that give a wall's top (walls.barriers' class rows, the curtain's values, V07 §3.4's village rows): an edit that moves a soffit or a wall's top re-checks each crossing whose form, clearance or cap it changes by §2.7's laws (law 4; law 1 (2), (5), (7), (10)), as stripMarginM's does'; scope (E-S13's T110-4 (c)): the drawn edits add 'raisedWays.structure.span.deckDepthCm and a walls.barriers height row'; V12 (E-V12-1 widened): the span-rule line's readers add '§2.7's laws, law 1 (2), (5), (7)'.
